As with the p orbitals, we take linear combinations of the angular wave functions to obtain orbitals with specific orientations relative to the Cartesian axes. The conventionally chosen linear combinations of the solutions with m 5 22, 21, 11, 12 give four orbitals with the same shape but dif­ferent orientations with respect to the Cartesian axes: dxy, dyz, dxz, and dx y 2 2 − (Fig. 5.13). For example, a dxy orbital has four lobes, two with positive phase and two with negative phase; the maximum amplitude is at 45° to the x- and y-axes.
